title: Self-Driving Cars
objective: After this level you can explain how self-driving cars sense the road around them.
summary: Self-driving cars combine cameras, radar, lidar, GPS and detailed maps. SAE Levels 0-5 say who is driving; a Level 3 system went on sale in California in 2023.

cards.headline: On October 8, 2020, the public could ride in a car with no driver at all.
cards.body: That day Waymo opened its fully driverless ride service, with no one at the wheel, to the public in the Phoenix area. To drive with no human, a car has to do what you do all the time without noticing: see everything around it, and know where it is.

cards.headline: Seeing with timers
cards.body: A self-driving car carries cameras, radar and lidar, plus GPS and highly detailed maps of its roads. Radar works just like Level 35's: time the radio echo. Lidar does the same with pulses of laser light, measuring the distance to whatever each pulse bounces off. Computers fuse it all into a 3-D map of the surroundings and keep adjusting steering, speed and braking.

items.label: Levels 0-2
points: You are driving, even when features help
You must supervise all the time

items.label: Level 3
points: The car drives in limited conditions
You must take over when it asks

items.label: Levels 4-5
points: Level 4 needs no takeover within its limits

cards.fact: In 2023, California approved a Level 3 system for sale to the public.
cards.context: On June 8, 2023, the state approved Mercedes-Benz Drive Pilot: highways only, daylight only, up to 40 mph, and the driver must stay behind the wheel to take over when prompted. Britannica noted that, as of 2025, no car was fully autonomous. This field moves fast, so the date on any claim matters.

cards.headline: Self-driving: sensing
learned: Cameras, radar, lidar, GPS and detailed maps
Lidar times laser echoes, like radar with light
SAE Levels 0-2: you drive; 3-5: the system drives
A Level 3 system went on sale in California in 2023

questions.prompt: What does a self-driving car's lidar use to measure distance?

options.label: Signals from GPS satellites
options.rationale: GPS gives position, not distances to nearby objects.

questions.explanation: Lidar times reflected pulses of laser light to measure the distance to objects around the car.

questions.prompt: A car drives itself on the highway but asks you to take over when it reaches its limits. Which SAE level is that?

options.label: Level 2
options.rationale: At Level 2 you're driving the whole time.

options.label: Level 4
options.rationale: Level 4 doesn't need you to take over within its limits.

options.label: Level 5
options.rationale: Level 5 would never need a driver.

questions.explanation: Level 3: the system drives in limited conditions, but the human must take over when asked.

questions.prompt: Level 35's radar and a self-driving car's lidar both measure distance. How?

options.label: By reading a detailed map
options.rationale: Maps help, but they don't measure distance.

options.label: By timing how long a pulse takes to bounce back
By measuring the temperature of objects

questions.explanation: Radar times radio echoes and lidar times laser echoes; the round-trip time gives distance.
